one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is likely Q3 2026 earnings: Quanta reported Q3 2025 on Oct 30, 2025 (src 17), but no Q3 2026 date is posted on the IR calendar yet (src 18), so a late-October report (around Oct 29-30) is likely but not certain. Consensus for Q3 is EPS ~$4.99 on ~$10.9B revenue (src 3, 4), and it was revised up hard after the Q2 beat. Quanta beat Q2 by about 28% and the stock jumped ~16% (src 2), so the bar is now higher. Read-across from the industry is mixed: Hubbell and MYR saw T&D orders accelerate (src 6, 7), but MasTec fell 18.5% when backlog conversion slipped into 2027 (src 5), which shows how a timing miss gets punished. I expect a beat and a raise of the high end of guidance, but with a reaction of roughly +/-8-10% in either direction. So I used a distribution centred near spot (median ~665, slight upward tilt from the run of upward revisions) at monthly vol 44%/3.5 = 12.6%, with a 20% weight on a 1.6x-wider earnings-reaction component. The stock has already de-rated from 50x to 35x forward P/E (src 4), which limits further downside unless guidance disappoints.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of forward P/E ($694 = Oct-2027 NTM EPS ~$22.4 x 31x) and EV/EBITDA ($664 = NTM EBITDA ~$5.33B x 20x, less ~$5.0B net debt, / 153M shares). Fair value is about $680, 3% above spot.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus grown ~18%, the same as the implied FY26-27 consensus growth. Supported by $53.4B backlog (+36% YoY vs $39.2B), utility capex rising ~6-17%/yr, and equipment scarcity stretching the cycle out rather than ending it.

PWR is at ~35x today, down from ~50x at the end of June. Peers: EMCOR ~31x, Sterling ~43x, MasTec ~47x. I assume some further de-rating as growth normalises toward high teens, and set it at the low end of the peer range because of Quanta's scale, its 80-85% self-perform share and its utility-heavy mix.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA as of Oct 2027 ~$5.33B x 20x = EV $106.6B; less net debt ~$5.0B; / 153M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus revenue x ~10.5% EBITDA margin (2026 guidance implies ~10.5%; management sees electric segment margins of 10-12% possible). 2028 grows ~15% on backlog conversion: large transmission and generation field work starts in 2H27.
Current EV ~$106.6B (662.6 x 152.4M shares + $5.6B net debt) / NTM EBITDA ~$4.64B = ~23x. I take it down to 20x, in line with the P/E de-rating assumption and peers' multiples.
Reported net debt, less FCF ($2.0-2.5B guidance), plus continued M&A (~$1.5B+/yr, like the four Q2 deals at $1.24B upfront).
Slight creep from stock compensation and acquisition consideration.

bear.story: AI and data-center capex pauses or is financed less easily, state moratoria and large-load tariffs (NY, OK, NJ) slow interconnections, and the EO 14420 equipment ban plus transformer shortages push transmission work into 2028, the same timing slippage MasTec was punished for. EPS growth slows to ~10%, NTM EPS ~$20, and the multiple falls to ~22x.

base.story: Backlog converts on schedule, 2027 EPS comes in near $20, large transmission and generation field work starts in 2H27, and utility capex keeps growing high single to low double digits. The multiple compresses to ~31x on NTM ~$22.5.

bull.story: Quanta keeps beating consensus as it did in Q2 (+28%). Hyperscaler capex for 2027 rises 'significantly' (Alphabet) toward $1T+, and the labor bottleneck (Bernstein) gives Quanta pricing power. NTM EPS reaches ~$24.5 and the multiple holds ~38x.

thesis_break_reason: $470 is ~29% below spot and ~24x FY27 consensus EPS ($19.77), about 16% above the 52-week low ($404.51), which was set before backlog grew ~36% and estimates were revised up ~20%. Getting there would most likely need a real fundamental break: a guidance cut, backlog falling sequentially, or a visible pause in hyperscaler and utility capex (e.g. rate cases rejected, data-center tariffs halting large-load interconnects). Normal 44%-vol drift would not usually take it there with estimates still being revised up.

reasoning: Facts: Q2 2026 adj. EPS $4.24 vs $3.31 consensus, FY26 guidance raised to $16.45-16.95, backlog $53.4B (+36% YoY), net debt $5.6B, 152.4M diluted shares. Consensus FY27 EPS is $19.77, up from $16.49 60 days ago. On the industry side, the chain confirms demand. Hubbell's T&S orders are up sharply with book-to-bill 1.2x, MYR backlog is +19.6%, MasTec Power Delivery backlog is a record $6.3B, EEI shows IOU capex of ~$239B in 2026 (+17%) and $1.4T through 2030, and S&P puts utility capex near $1.3T for 2026-30. Hyperscalers signal higher 2027 capex. The Manifold market on 2027 big-4 capex resolved N/A, but its last pricing was 48% for >$800B on thin volume, which I treat as sentiment only. The risks come from the same chain. MasTec fell 18.5% on backlog timing slipping into 2027. Wood Mackenzie sees a 15% transformer shortage, and EO 14420 (effective for transactions after Aug 26, 2026) restricts foreign >=69kV equipment. Over 300 state data-center bills have been filed, with moratoria in NY and OK. Labor is the bottleneck, which Bernstein argues favors Quanta's scale. Valuation: the P/E and EV/EBITDA blend gives $680, close to spot, because I assume the multiple keeps compressing from 35x toward ~31x and earnings growth offsets most of that. The analyst mean target of ~$770 is higher than mine. Scenarios: 22% at $440, 53% at $700, 25% at $930, which gives a mean of ~$700. Ladder: a lognormal mixture with median ~$685, 85% weight at sigma 0.38 and 15% at sigma 0.65 for the fat tails of an AI-linked high-multiple name. That is slightly below the 44% realized vol for the core and wider in the tails, consistent with a ~25-35% large-cap base rate scaled up for this stock. Research limit: S&P and some peer pages were blocked or headline-only; X was not used.
